Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comment: The source says: "the K’Chò 1st and 2nd person verbal indexations, show nominative-accusative." but in flagging is ergative alignment.
curated_comment: Verified against Mang 2006:16-18. Flagging is ergative-absolutive: A takes ERG 'noh', S and P are unmarked/absolutive. 1st person pronoun as A is marked 'noh' (ex.8a Keini noh ... 1DL.ERG), while 1st person as P is bare (ex.9b keimi '1PL' object, unmarked). So A=ERG, S=P=ABS. Not tripartite (no accusative marking on pronouns). The nom-acc split reported in Mang 2006:20 is in VERBAL INDEXATION, not flagging, so it does not affect this feature. Coding 1 confirmed.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
curated_comment: Verified against Mang 2006:16-18. 2nd person pronoun as A is marked ERG 'noh' (ex.9a Nangni noh ... 2DL.ERG), while 2nd person as P is bare (ex.8b nangmi '2PL' object, unmarked). A=ERG, S=P=ABS -> ergative-absolutive, not tripartite. Coding 1 confirmed.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
Comment: It is possible to assume that due the previous note, but it is not stated in the source, nor can any examples be found.
curated_comment: Resolved from '?' to 1 by structural inference. Ergative 'noh' is a general nominal case clitic (Mang 2006:16) with no person-conditioned split in flagging; the only person sensitivity in the language is in verbal indexation (Mang 2006:20), which GB409 flagging features do not measure. 3rd-person referents (nouns) canonically take 'noh' (ex.6 Ui noh) and 1st/2nd pronouns take 'noh', so 3rd-person pronouns are inferred to do likewise -> erg-abs, not tripartite. NOTE: no free 3sg pronoun token with 'noh' is attested in the grammar; revert to '?' if strict attestation is required.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
curated_comment: Verified against Mang 2006:16 (sec.1.5.4, ex.5-6). Nouns: S unmarked (ex.5 Vok 'pig' died), A marked ERG 'noh' (ex.6 Ui noh 'dog.ERG'), P unmarked (ex.6 vok 'pig'). S=P=ABS, A=ERG -> ergative-absolutive, not tripartite. Coding 1 confirmed.
